letter.entry.aria: Tesseract · A letter for users{unread, select, yes { · unread} other {}}
letter.palette.label: Open the letter for users
letter.p1.what: It looks after your connection: it lines your nodes up like a relay, and when one can't get through, it moves on to the next by itself. You don't have to keep watch.
letter.p1.about: This letter is only a few pages long: how to get started, and a few things worth keeping in mind.
letter.p2.title: Three steps to start
letter.p2.import: On the “{tiers}” page, click “{import}” and add your nodes or a subscription URL.
letter.p2.tray: You can close the window: Tesseract stays in the notification area at the bottom right of the taskbar and keeps working.
letter.p3.title: One tier after another
letter.p3.vanguard: Vanguard holds your own nodes, such as a server you set up yourself. Most of the time, traffic goes here.
letter.p3.sentinel: Sentinel holds the nodes from your subscriptions. It takes over when no Vanguard node gets through.
letter.p3.bastion: Bastion is the last resort. It uses public nodes collected from the internet; turn it on only when you need it.
letter.p3.gateway: Gateway is a fixed exit: use it when websites should always see the same address. If you don't need that, leave it alone.
letter.p3.relay: When one tier runs into trouble, traffic moves on to the next by itself, and comes back once it recovers.
letter.p4.title: Two ways to capture traffic
letter.p4.system: {system}: enough most of the time. Your browser and most apps go through Tesseract.
letter.p4.tun: {tun}: some apps ignore the system proxy, such as some games and command-line tools. Turn this on and all traffic on this computer goes through Tesseract. It needs Tesseract to be run as an administrator.
letter.p4.drift: If another proxy app changes the system proxy, “{overview}” will say so. Close that app, then click “{restart}”.
letter.p5.title: A few things to keep in mind
letter.p5.ks: {ks}: when every tier is down, it holds your traffic back so your real IP isn't exposed. Unless you have a good reason, leave it on.
letter.p5.bastion: Bastion nodes come from the internet, and nobody knows who runs them. While traffic goes through Bastion, don't sign in to accounts or type passwords.
letter.p5.bundle: A diagnostic bundle contains the sites and IP addresses you visited. Look it over before you send it to anyone.
letter.p6.title: One last thing
letter.p6.search: Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd> to search for any setting or action.
letter.p6.logs: If something goes wrong, look at “{logs}” first. If you need someone's help, you can export a diagnostic bundle there.
letter.p6.again: To read this letter again, click Tesseract at the top left.
